title: Tuala Merah
mood: tender, proud and a little lovesick
subject: a tower-crane operator on a Bukit Jalil building site who watches his flat through cheap binoculars from the cab forty storeys up, where his wife hangs a red towel on the balcony rail at noon every day
caption: Romantic bolero, a slow Latin ballad with mariachi trumpets. A nylon-string requinto guitar playing ornamented runs between the lines; a second nylon guitar strumming the bolero rhythm; bongos and maracas keeping the bolero pattern soft and steady; two mariachi trumpets answering in thirds at the end of each chorus; a string section holding long notes and swelling into the choruses. Warm live-room recording, guitars and voice close, trumpets slightly back with a natural hall tail, strings soft and wide. Male baritone crooner, warm and close to the mic, stretching phrases with gentle rubato and opening up in the chorus. 80 BPM, A minor. Tender, proud and a little lovesick, forty storeys up. No piano, no trap beat, no reggaeton dembow, no autotune, no synth pads, no rock drum kit.
lyrics:
[Intro - requinto guitar run and soft strings]

[Verse 1]
Pukul tujuh aku panjat tangga besi
Empat puluh tingkat, langit KL masih kelabu
Dari kabin kren semua nampak kecil
Lori simen, topi kuning, kereta beratur

[Pre-Chorus]
Teropong murah beli kat Petaling Street
Aku cari tingkat sembilan, balkoni ketiga

[Chorus]
Tuala merah di pagar balkoni
Kau sidai tepat tengah hari
Orang lain nampak kain basah
Aku dengar, "Abang, saya kat sini"

[Verse 2]
Isnin lepas hujan turun dari subuh
Kerja berhenti, aku duduk dalam kabin
Pukul dua belas aku tak harap apa-apa
Tapi merah itu naik juga, basah lencun

[Chorus]
Tuala merah di pagar balkoni
Kau sidai juga dalam hujan lebat
Orang lain nampak kain basah
Aku dengar, "Abang, saya tunggu"

[Bridge - trumpets and strings swell]
Hari ni ada kain lain kat sebelah
Mandur panggil, aku langsung tak dengar

[Chorus]
Tuala merah di pagar balkoni
Dan sehelai baju kecil warna putih
Orang lain nampak kain basah
Aku dengar, "Abang, kita dah bertiga"

[Outro - requinto guitar and trumpets, fading]
